conditions.description: Long coastal voyage down to Egypt
Memphis is expensive to operate in

special_event.description: First time approaching Memphis the player sees the Nile river delta — a unique visual moment, the sea turns brown-green from river sediment. A one-time discovery flag triggers.

tile_details.description: fine pale dust and flat stone paving — drier and dustier than anything on the coast
brown-green river water visible at the dock edge, flowing slowly
Egyptian architecture — flat-topped, painted with hieroglyphs, massive scale
noticeably shabbier — foreign merchants kept in a separate, less grand part of the city
enormous walls with guard towers. No entry. Visible from most of the map as a backdrop.

day.note: Harsh bright sunlight — brightest in the game. No coastal moisture to soften it.

location.lore_note: Memphis is the most powerful city in the game world — but the player experiences none of that power directly. As a foreigner, they are confined largely to the foreign quarter and the market. The Egyptians are polite but condescending. Everything costs more here. The bureaucracy is real. But the goods available and the information accessible here cannot be found anywhere else.

visual.description: A long stone dock on the Nile. Egyptian dock workers are efficient and unfriendly to foreigners. An inspection booth at the entrance examines all cargo.

services.note: Higher than anywhere else — Egypt taxes foreigners heavily

services.description: Mandatory inspection of all incoming cargo. Contraband confiscated.

services.note: Most expensive repair in the game. Egypt does nothing cheaply for foreigners.

visual.description: Enormous and imposing. Stone stalls with painted hieroglyph labels. Every transaction recorded by a scribe in a booth. Tax collectors move through the market constantly. Everything is formal, organized, and slightly intimidating.

best_selling_items_here.description: Egypt will pay top price for these Phoenician goods

buildings.note: Egypt is the single best destination for cedar and glass. Every run to Memphis with a full hold of cedar is one of the most profitable trades in the game.

visual.description: A building that functions as both a government permit office and a private scroll market. Clerks and scribes work at every desk. The smell of papyrus and ink is stronger here than anywhere except Byblos.

services.benefit: Removes 15% market tax for current Memphis visit. Valid for 7 days.
services.note: If player plans to sell a large valuable cargo, this permit pays for itself immediately

effect.note: Illegal to possess. Confiscated if caught in cargo inspection.

effect.description: Unlocks ability to interact with Egyptian inscriptions in ruins

visual.description: Massive. The player cannot enter — the main temple is for Egyptians only. But the outer court is accessible to foreigners who make a proper offering. Enormous painted stone columns visible from outside. Guards in formal Egyptian armor.

lines.speaker: kha
lines.text: Foreign merchant. Dock fee is 25 silver. Cargo inspection is mandatory. Do you have a trade permit? No? Market tax is 15 percent. Welcome to Memphis.

lines.speaker: kha
lines.text: You brought a letter from my cousin in Byblos. He speaks well of you.

lines.speaker: kha
lines.text: I will waive your first inspection fee. And I will tell the market scribes you are a trusted contact. That is worth more than silver here.

ongoing_service.description: After the letter quest, Kha gives the player a weekly tip about which Egyptian goods are in highest demand that week

lines.speaker: userhat
lines.text: Quietly. Don't make it obvious you're talking to me.

lines.speaker: userhat
lines.text: I have maps I shouldn't have. You want maps you shouldn't have. I think we can help each other.

secret.description: Was dismissed from the royal court's map archive for making unauthorized copies. He still has contacts inside who pass him new survey maps of Egypt's trade routes.

entry_position.description: An old sealed hatch at the base of the dock wall — a forgotten storage vault from an older version of the dock

discovery_triggers.description: Kha mentions the old vault in passing after trusting the player
Player finds the hatch while exploring near the water line

options.description: Kha gives a key if disposition is high enough

contents.description: A forgotten storage vault. Old grain long since rotted. But the walls have painted records — trade records from centuries ago.
Detailed records of trade routes used by Egypt 500 years ago — including one route going far south along the African coast
contents.note: If player already has Hanno Minor's Africa expedition map from Carthage, these records confirm the same southern route — double evidence

reward_summary.note: No map fragment here — Memphis rewards are economic and informational rather than voyage-critical

steps.description: Map must be hidden in cargo to pass inspection

options.description: Keep map — reveals Red Sea route for Part 2
Sell to Sidon guild for 500 silver
Sell to Tyre high priest for 600 silver

steps.description: Kha offers a standing contract: deliver cedar to Memphis every 15 in-game days

reward_per_delivery.note: On top of normal market price. Makes Memphis the single most profitable cedar destination in the game for regular traders.

economy.note: Memphis is the single most profitable destination for Phoenician manufactured goods — especially cedar, glass, and purple dye. But the high docking fee and 15% tax mean you need to bring a full, valuable cargo to make the long voyage worthwhile.
